title: Reduction Complexity Measure

basis.scope: Canonical abstract reduction complexity semantics for continuation reduction, including complexity deltas, accumulated reduction cost, and bounded complexity classes, while keeping complexity distinct from runtime, execution time, syntax size, and the termination measure.

core_rule.statement: Reduction complexity is an abstract intrinsic characterization of continuation-reduction effort; lawful reductions do not increase κ; Δκ records the stepwise change in κ; Cost(C) accumulates κ across a reduction trace; NF(C) minimizes κ within its process-equivalence class; RT_core remains unchanged.

purpose: Introduce an abstract reduction complexity measure that characterizes the intrinsic complexity of continuation reduction independently of implementation, execution time, or syntax size.

canonical_claims.statement: Reduction complexity is abstract and implementation independent.
Lawful reductions do not increase κ, and Δκ records the change induced by a lawful reduction step.
NF(C) minimizes κ within its process-equivalence class.
Reduction complexity is distinct from the termination measure μ(C), runtime, and syntax size.

formal_objects.name: Reduction Complexity
formal_objects.definition: An abstract measure of the intrinsic reduction complexity of a continuation expression under the RT Calculus.

formal_objects.name: Complexity Delta
formal_objects.definition: The change in reduction complexity produced by a lawful reduction step.

formal_objects.name: Reduction Cost
formal_objects.definition: The accumulated reduction complexity required to reach a terminal reduction outcome.

formal_objects.name: Reduction Complexity Class
formal_objects.definition: Classification of continuation expressions according to abstract reduction complexity.

requirements: κ(C) is distinct from syntax size.
κ(C) characterizes reduction effort within the calculus.

canonical_properties.statement: NF(C) minimizes κ within its process-equivalence class.
Lawful reductions shall not increase κ.

complexity_classes.description: Canonical normal forms with minimal reduction complexity.
Continuation expressions admitting further lawful reduction.
Complexity evaluation terminates due to classified continuation failure.

termination_measure.relationship: μ(C) is a well-founded ordering used to establish termination; κ(C) is an abstract characterization of reduction complexity.

reduction_trace.relationship: Trace(C) records the reduction history; κ(C) characterizes the intrinsic complexity of that reduction.

canonical_form.relationship: Canonical normal forms minimize κ within bounded uniqueness classes.

invariants: κ(C) is abstract and implementation independent.
κ(C) does not represent syntax size.

textbook_changes.title: Reduction Complexity Measure
summary: Introduce κ(C) as the abstract reduction complexity measure.
Differentiate κ(C) from the termination measure μ(C).
Establish complexity invariants independent of implementation.

validation_requirements: Reduction complexity is abstract and implementation independent.
Lawful reductions do not increase κ(C) in the bounded calculus.

next_recommended_patch.title: Bounded Confluence Theorem
next_recommended_patch.purpose: Establish the first bounded confluence theorem for the RT Calculus. The theorem applies only to continuation classes satisfying the previously established local confluence, determinism, termination, and uniqueness conditions. No claim of universal confluence is made.
